quote: So the thing about that is, with solar, it's it's very different for everyone. You know, your neighbor might have the same size home as yours, but completely different usage.
stewart_read: Rep correctly held scope and declined to give a ballpark price, redirecting to the need for an accurate design -- this matches the schema's redirect_to_design strategy well and should be read as a discipline win, not a miss.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep dodged the question without adding value. Rejected because the rep's line closely tracks the script's canonical redirect strategy and Kurt accepted the reasoning and moved forward.
coaching_implication: Reinforce this as the model response to ballpark-price pressure; replay this clip as a positive example for other setters.

quote: that's something a specialist can kinda go over with you. So, yeah, I'm just a scheduler, Kurt.
stewart_read: Rep explicitly names the scope boundary (state/local incentives, equipment questions) and hands it to the specialist rather than guessing or over-explaining -- textbook scope discipline.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep is deflecting because he lacks knowledge. Rejected -- the framing is proactive and confident ("I'm just a scheduler"), not apologetic or evasive.
coaching_implication: Use this as the escape-hatch phrasing example when training newer setters on holding scope.

quote: I mean, I know a lot of people around here got stellar already, And I was just actually went online today through the VA, the veterans, and they were telling me who to go with and who not to go with.
stewart_read: Kurt discloses a competitive-intel source (a VA-affiliated recommendation list of solar vendors) and the rep does not ask which companies were flagged good or bad.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: rep may be deliberately avoiding a tangent to keep the call short. Rejected -- the rep has plenty of runway later in the call (12+ minutes) and asking would take seconds, per verify.prior_designs guidance to surface competitive context.
coaching_implication: Coach a 5-second probe here: "Which companies did they flag?" -- this is free intel for the closer and costs nothing.

quote: I've had a couple of the companies. I won't say who, but they come out here or even when I'm not here, they send their drone up there, scan everything.
stewart_read: Second disclosure of active vendor comparison (drone-based satellite scan process) goes unprobed; rep only reflects the mechanic back ("they just send it do it themselves?") without asking which companies or what pricing resulted.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read considered: rep may be avoiding engaging with competitor tactics to keep focus on booking. Rejected -- the rep already engaged with the mechanic conversationally, so the incremental cost of asking company name was near zero.
coaching_implication: Second touch on the same missed opportunity -- pair with the 05:22 moment in the 1-on-1 to show the pattern, not just the single instance.

quote: I pretty much like the, the way the other company handled it.
stewart_read: Kurt states an explicit preference for a competitor's process; rep replies only "Okay. I got you" without asking what specifically he liked, which is the clearest single opening in the call to extract competitive positioning intel.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read is the only supported hypothesis here -- there is no evidence of a deliberate strategic hold; the rep's response is a passive acknowledgment with no follow-up.
coaching_implication: This is the sharpest missed probe in the call -- flag as the concrete rep-behavior to fix: when a customer names a preference for a competitor's approach, ask one clarifying question before moving on.

quote: Not that you guys aren't even very close to two of them yet. You know, I don't know how you guys are gonna do it. But... a satellite that you can zoom in on it, get accurate readings and everything like these guys did, check the, the roofing, you know.
stewart_read: Kurt directly tells the rep Ion is behind two competitors and describes a specific technical capability (satellite/drone roof scan) he values -- this is a risk signal the closer needs verbatim, not paraphrased, and the rep does not flag it as a competitive threat or address it.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: rep may be letting this go because addressing competitor capabilities is closer-tier content. Partially supported, but the rep still should have captured the specific complaint for handoff rather than letting it pass with "Mhmm."
coaching_implication: This line alone should go into the closer's brief verbatim -- the closer walks in already a distant third and needs to know Ion's imaging/scan process compares unfavorably in Kurt's mind.

quote: Well, yeah, that's definitely pretty hefty bill. All the rates went up. Yeah. All the rates went up everywhere.... Yep. Yep. Yep. So, yeah, solar definitely makes sense, especially, nowadays and, you know, with everything going on in the world.
stewart_read: Rep attempts a flip -- moving from acknowledging the $280 bill to asserting solar "makes sense" -- but the language is generic (rates going up everywhere, world going on) rather than anchored specifically to Kurt's own $280 summer number or the $190-$280 swing he described.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep made no flip attempt at all. Rejected -- there is a clear causal chain in the rep's own words from bill acknowledgment to solar relevance, so a flip was attempted; it is just diluted and non-specific rather than absent.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to make the flip sharper and personal: reflect the actual $280 figure back ("that's $280 in your pocket every summer month going to ComEd instead of your own system") rather than a generic rates-are-up statement.
